Copy at literature/sources/winkler-2026-ferrers-gap-polynomials-2026-09-18.pdf. THE PRIOR-ART RISK THIS ENTRY WAS OPENED FOR IS DISCHARGED, AND THE TITLE WAS MISLEADING IN OUR FAVOUR. WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: a pure enumerative-combinatorics paper about Ferrers gap polynomials, not a Collatz paper. For a partition eta, G_eta(y) sums y^|I(mu)| over partitions mu contained in eta, where I(mu) indexes the adjacent-part drops of size at least 2. Support is the independent sets of a nested or Schubert matroid (Proposition 2, reproved from the first-passage paper). Substituting y = 1 + z gives a marked boundary-path model with steps (1,0), (0,1) and (2,1), hence exact full-column, new-row and bottom-row recurrences. THEOREM 1 is the whole result: for a partition with AT MOST FIVE POSITIVE PARTS, every zero of a nonconstant G_eta is simple and negative, and adding a full column gives strict oriented interlacing. Three rows by an exact Gram-matrix certificate, four rows by finite Stieltjes-Newton chains, five rows by a two-column strengthening plus diagonal-tail interlacing and degree-by-degree Stieltjes analysis. Appendices A-E are the exact Wronskian, Gram, Newton and Stieltjes certificates, with a reproducibility archive called Online Resource 1. WHY IT DOES NOT TOUCH PAPER B. There is exactly one Collatz section, 3.1, one page long, and he says twice that the specialization is not used in any proof and that the real-zero problem is intrinsic to Ferrers shapes and independent of the Collatz interpretation. In it, alpha = log2 3, rho = alpha - 1, h_k = floor(k/rho) + 1, Lambda(n) = (n - h_1, ..., n - h_(q_n)) with q_n = floor(n rho), and B_n(y) = G_Lambda(n)(y) is the cut polynomial of the coefficient first-passage words, so B_n is the refinement of A100982 = our M_d. COROLLARY 35 is the Beatty column recurrence, P_(n,t) = P_(n,t-1) + P_(n-1,t) + [n >= h_t + 2](y-1) P_(n-2,t-1), and with H_(n,t)(z) = P_(n,t)(1+z) the same with z H_(n-2,t-1); its three terms are the north, east and long step of the path model, and the Beatty boundary enters only through h_(t+1) - h_t in {1,2}. THEN IT STOPS. Real-rootedness and interlacing for the Beatty family are CONJECTURE 36, for all n >= 4, verified only for 4 <= n < 60 by rational root isolation; the general shape statement is CONJECTURE 34. CRITICALLY, THEOREM 1 REACHES ALMOST NONE OF OUR RANGE: at most five positive parts means q_n = floor(n rho) <= 5, i.e. n <= 10, since rho = 0.5849625. There is no asymptotic statement anywhere in the paper, no growth constant, no central limit theorem and no oscillation. So it neither proves nor approaches the limit layer Paper B claims, and the hedge recorded here from the title alone was right. PROJECT RELATIONSHIP is therefore 'known', not a competitor. WHAT IS WORTH TAKING. Conjecture 36 is four days old and verified to n < 60 with degree q_n about 0.585 n, so degree 34 at n = 60. This laboratory computes these counts to word length 900 and could isolate roots well past n = 200, where the degree is 116. Extending his newest conjecture is a cheap and concrete thing to offer him, and better than the 2015 offer currently in the draft email. He also records that the zero-trimmed Beatty growth was checked through n = 500 and that exactly 116 of the transitions 2 <= n < 200 create one new row of length 1, both independently checkable here. Corollary 35 was implemented independently from the paper text in tmp/ferrers_beatty_check.py: B_n(1) reproduces all 32 stored terms of A100982 at offset zero, while offsets +1, -1 and +2 give 1/31, 1/32 and 0/30, so the alignment is checked and not assumed; the constant terms also come out as his power-of-two law. tmp/ferrers_conj36.py then isolates the real roots exactly with sympy and tests strict oriented interlacing. CONJECTURE 36 HOLDS FOR EVERY 4 <= n <= 120, against the 4 <= n < 60 he records, with no failure, every zero real simple and negative, and a negative control that rejects the reversed orientation on 59 of 59 equal-degree pairs. Degree of B_120 is 59. Total runtime 98 seconds, so 200 is reachable in minutes and the limit is patience, not method. This is a verification of his conjecture, not a proof of it, and it is his result to use. SENT TO THE AUTHOR, 22 September 2026.
